Every Janmashtami, millions of people stay awake until exactly midnight... to rock a tiny cradle. Why midnight? Because of a prison. Mathura, long ago. King Kamsa hears a prophecy: his sister's eighth son will end him.
So he locks his sister Devaki and her husband Vasudeva in a prison. Iron chains. Guards at every door. And he waits.
Then, on a stormy night, at exactly midnight, the eighth son is born. Tiny. Blue. Smiling. Krishna.
Wait, so how does a baby escape a prison? The chains fall off. The guards fall asleep. And the doors swing open by themselves.
Vasudeva puts the baby in a basket and walks into the storm. The river Yamuna is flooding. Then a giant serpent rises behind him... and spreads its hoods like an umbrella.
That's why, even today, temples wait until midnight. The conch blows, the cradle rocks, and everyone sings: he's here. Comment Jai Shri Krishna if you stayed up for him.
